en: to Maheśvara, who wears a necklace of serpent-kings, who has three eyes, and whose body is smeared with ashes!
Salutations to that Śiva, who is eternal, pure, and sky-clad, and who is denoted by the syllable "Na. || 1 ||
To Maheśvara, the lord of Nandīśvara and the Pramathas, who is anointed with the waters of the Mandākinī and sandalwood paste,
and who is well-worshipped with Mandāra flowers and many other blossoms.
Salutation to that Ma-kāra, who is Śiva. || 2 ||
To Śiva, who is like the sun to the multitude of lotus-faces of Gaurī; to the destroyer of Dakṣa’s sacrifice;
to the illustrious Nīlakaṇṭha, whose banner is the bull.
Salutation to that Śikāra, who is Śiva. || 3 ||
To him whose crest is worshipped by the gods— the lords of sages such as Vasiṣṭha, Agastya (Kumbhodbhava), and Gautama—
and whose eyes are the moon, the sun, and the fire.
Salutation to that Vakāra, who is Śiva. || 4 ||
To the one whose form is that of a yakṣa, who wears matted locks, who holds a trident in his hand, the eternal,
the divine, the god who is clothed in the directions.
Salutation to that Yakāra, who is Śiva. || 5 ||
Whoever recites these five syllables, which are meritorious, in the presence of Śiva,
attains the world of Śiva and rejoices together with Śiva.
Thus ends the Śivapañcākṣarastotra composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
